My overall reading If Carson asks: "What can we still hear when Sappho's poem is broken?" Cranes asks a slightly different question: "What happens when the broken poem continues speaking?" And Day and Night answers by making translation itself an erotic act: something ancient encounters something contemporary, crosses into another language, changes form, loses things, gains things—and nevertheless continues to desire.
